page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server within the n1 family, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM. The processing power is delivered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, featuring 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. This server does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1125.48 and multi-core score of 2941.66 are categorized as weak, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 21.69 GB/sec for large block writes. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds are poor, registering at 18.99 GB/sec and 7.16 GB/sec respectively.

From a workload perspective, the server is constrained by its low memory allocation of 0.9 GB per core. It is suitable for lightweight compute tasks that do not require large memory footprints, such as basic static web serving, which benchmarked at 2.92 GB/sec, or simple database operations. It is not suitable for memory-intensive applications, large-scale software compilation, or complex LLM inference, as demonstrated by its poor performance on small 135M model prompt processing.
